suggestions.title: Quantum Mechanics: Spin, Perturbation, and Scattering
suggestions.description_md:
The apparatus required to read modern atomic, condensed-matter, and
particle physics — angular momentum and spin developed properly,
time-independent and time-dependent perturbation theory, scattering
theory, identical particles and quantum statistics, and density
matrices for handling mixed states. Where the introductory pass
introduces the Schrödinger equation and solves a handful of canonical
problems, this builds the toolkit that working theorists actually use.
suggestions.why_suggested_md: Builds on the quantum foundations you flagged; spin and perturbation theory are essential for statistical mechanics of many-body systems.

suggestions.title: Partial Differential Equations
suggestions.description_md:
The mathematics of fields that vary in space and time — heat diffusing
through a metal bar, waves spreading on a drum head, the electrostatic
potential around a charge, the Schrödinger evolution of a quantum state.
Builds the classification into hyperbolic, parabolic, and elliptic
equations, the canonical solution techniques (separation of variables,
Fourier methods, Green's functions, method of characteristics), and the
qualitative differences in behaviour each class produces.
suggestions.why_suggested_md: Heat diffusion and field equations underpin both thermodynamics and the path-integral formulation of statistical mechanics you'll need.

suggestions.title: Lagrangian Mechanics
suggestions.description_md:
A reformulation of classical mechanics that replaces forces with the
principle of least action — every classical trajectory is the one
that extremises a single integral, and the equations of motion fall
out as the Euler-Lagrange conditions. Beyond elegance, this framework
generalises naturally to constrained systems, fields, and (eventually)
the path integral formulation of quantum mechanics, while Noether's
theorem reveals conservation laws as direct consequences of the
symmetries of the Lagrangian.
suggestions.why_suggested_md: The action principle connects classical mechanics to partition functions and path integrals in statistical mechanics naturally.

suggestions.title: Electromagnetism: Dynamics and Radiation
suggestions.description_md:
The full machinery of classical electromagnetism once the source
charges and currents are moving — Maxwell's equations in matter, the
propagation of electromagnetic waves, radiation from accelerating
charges, and the gauge structure that anticipates modern field
theory. Where the static-fields pass gives you Coulomb, Gauss, and
Faraday's law of induction, this builds the dynamical and
relativistic structure: Poynting's theorem, dipole and multipole
radiation, waveguides, and the covariant formulation that makes
Lorentz invariance manifest.
suggestions.why_suggested_md: Completes your electromagnetism refresh with dynamics; field theory language carries directly into statistical field theory.

suggestions.title: Complex Analysis
suggestions.description_md:
The calculus of functions of a complex variable, where the constraint
of differentiability is so strong it forces analytic functions to be
uniquely determined by their values on any small disk. Builds toward
contour integration, the residue theorem, and the deep connection
between the complex plane and physics — conformal maps in fluid
dynamics, Cauchy's integral formula as a tool throughout theoretical
physics, and analytic continuation as a window onto the structure of
special functions.
suggestions.why_suggested_md: Essential for contour integration in partition function calculations and phase transition singularities you'll encounter.

suggestions.title: Semiconductor Physics
suggestions.description_md: Semiconductor physics explains how crystalline materials with a moderate band gap give rise to controllable electrical behavior through doping, carrier transport, and junction formation. It bridges quantum mechanics and solid-state theory to explain why silicon can act as a switch, a diode, or an amplifier depending on how it is structured and biased. Anyone who wants to understand transistors, solar cells, or LEDs at a physical rather than circuit level needs this foundation.
suggestions.why_suggested_md: The Ising model and band structure share deep roots in condensed-matter statistical mechanics; a natural application domain.

suggestions.title: Special Relativity
suggestions.description_md:
Einstein's 1905 reformulation of space and time as a single
four-dimensional structure in which the speed of light is invariant
and simultaneity is observer-dependent. The Lorentz transformations
replace Galilean ones, mass-energy equivalence emerges as a kinematic
identity, and electromagnetism becomes geometrically natural —
Maxwell's equations are already Lorentz-invariant. The conceptual
on-ramp to general relativity and the geometric language used
throughout modern field theory.
suggestions.why_suggested_md: Provides the relativistic extension of classical mechanics; useful context for understanding field theory foundations later.
